solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: It's presently mostly against Conservatives local wing involving Lithium company

definitions.note: a topical description rather than a synonym: 'it' is the answer

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it in, so one part is wrapped round another

parts.note: a local is a pub, the one nearest your home
Li is the chemical symbol for lithium
Co is the standard abbreviation for company
a pinion is a bird's wing

explanation.surface: A satirical jab: voters these days are mostly turning against the Tories, even the local wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local wing' reads as a party branch, but local means the neighbourhood pub and wing is a bird's pinion; the element and firm abbreviations sit between them.
explanation.definitionFit: What the population broadly thinks is described here by its current political mood, polls running heavily against the governing party.

clue.text: A French-style attack is feeble

parts.note: un is the French for 'a'
a fit is a sudden attack, as of coughing

explanation.surface: A put-down of some Gallic manner of assault as limp and ineffective.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French-style' tells you to translate 'A' into French; 'attack' is the medical kind, a seizure.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone out of condition or lacking strength is weak and in poor physical shape, a synonym relation.

clue.text: Pinpointed pub on windy side

parts.note: a local is one's regular pub

indicators.note: windy suggests twisting and turning, so the letters wind into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A pub singled out for its exposed, blustery side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Windy' seems to describe the pub's side, but it is the signal to rearrange the word that follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pinpointed has been found at or confined to a precise spot, which is a synonym sense.

clue.text: Immense head of state in laughable setting

indicators.note: one thing placed in another is enclosed by it, so one part goes inside

parts.note: laughable means comic; 'setting' marks it as the outer part

indicators.note: a head is the top or front, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A huge national leader placed in a ridiculous situation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head of state' sounds like a president or monarch, but it is just the letter S.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmic means on the scale of the universe, so colloquially it means vast or enormous in size.

clue.text: Pop article on Mark, almost pitiable

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so a final letter is dropped

parts.note: pop and pa are both words for father
the definite article
a tick is a mark of approval; cut short it loses its K

explanation.surface: A pop music piece about someone called Mark that is nearly pitiful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop' looks like music but means dad; 'Mark' looks like a name but is a tick.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathetic and pitiable both describe something that arouses sorrow or contempt for its weakness; plain synonyms.

clue.text: Any two short names suitable for Rees-Mogg's minder?

indicators.note: suitable means made to fit, so the letters are arranged to suit

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for name, so two of them give two Ns

explanation.surface: A quiz-like question about which two nicknames would suit the MP's childhood carer.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacob Rees-Mogg, a Conservative MP, was famously raised by a nanny who stayed with the family for decades.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman employed to look after children is the carer the politician was well known for having into adulthood.

clue.text: Meddlesome, sub-standard, inept Conservative leaders with debts

parts.note: food or a performance that is off is below par

indicators.note: leaders are the ones at the front, so only the opening letters count

parts.note: the first letters of these two words
an IOU is a written acknowledgment of a debt

explanation.surface: An attack on interfering, incompetent Tory leaders who are running up debts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conservative leaders' reads as party chiefs, but 'leaders' takes only the initials of 'inept Conservative'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone officious is self-important and interfering, asserting authority where it is unwanted, a close synonym.

clue.text: In general is Somerset flexible?

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: run on from the end of the first word to the start of the third

explanation.surface: A question whether the West Country county of Somerset is, broadly speaking, adaptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In general' reads as 'on the whole', but 'In' means inside, and the answer runs across 'generaL IS SOMerset'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lissom describes a supple, lithe body that bends easily, so it is a synonym of pliant and bendy.

clue.text: Knob finally not stiff, so happy

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the closing letter is kept

parts.note: the last letter of the word
lithe means supple, the opposite of stiff

explanation.surface: A smutty Private Eye double entendre about relief once something is no longer rigid.
explanation.walkthrough: The innuendo is a distraction: 'Knob' just supplies its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Blithe means cheerful and carefree, a literary synonym for glad or contented.

clue.text: Resolved to get gen on conservative America

parts.note: gen is British slang for information, as is info
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
the US is America

explanation.surface: Someone determined to dig up information on right-wing America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resolved' looks like 'determined', but it is the optical sense: an image resolved is sharp.
explanation.definitionFit: In optics a resolved image shows clear detail, which is what a sharp, properly adjusted picture looks like.

clue.text: "Nut freaking out on liquid fuel" (Melody's description)

indicators.note: freaking out is losing control, so these letters go wild
liquid things flow and change shape, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tabloid-style headline about a crank losing it after drinking petrol, attributed to someone called Melody.
explanation.walkthrough: Both word groups are rearranged together; 'Melody' looks like a person quoted, but the answer is what describes a melody.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasing melody is described as tuneful, meaning musical and easy on the ear, an adjective for tunes.

clue.text: Was an MP chosen to bestride Labour leader and moon?

parts.note: an MP sits in Parliament, so one who was an MP sat

indicators.note: to bestride is to sit astride with legs on either side, so one part straddles another

parts.note: the elite are the chosen few

indicators.note: a leader goes first, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A cheeky question: was a former MP picked to straddle the Labour leader and show him a bare bottom?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moon' looks like a verb for baring buttocks, but it is the noun for a body orbiting a planet.
explanation.definitionFit: A natural satellite is a body in orbit round a planet, so every moon is an example of one.

clue.text: see 23 ac.
Think about lives getting ill-treatment

indicators.note: about means around, so one part goes round another

parts.note: to muse is to think or ponder
something that lives is, exists

explanation.surface: Pondering people's lives that are marked by cruelty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Think about' reads as one phrase, but 'Think' supplies the letters and 'about' says they wrap around the next piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Misuse as a noun means wrong or harmful handling, and ill-treatment is abuse of that kind: a synonym.

clue.text: Crawler churns out any PC tosh

indicators.note: churning stirs things up, so the letters come out mixed

parts.note: taken as written, nine letters

explanation.surface: A toady who produces any amount of politically correct rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: PC here is 'politically correct', not a police constable; its letters are simply part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A crawler is someone who fawns on superiors to win favour, exactly what a sycophant does.

clue.text: Leak: "former royal's meeting end"

parts.note: Diana, Princess of Wales, known as Di
the S of the possessive, taken as written
a close is an end or conclusion

explanation.surface: A tabloid leak about how a former royal met her end.
explanation.walkthrough: Princess Diana, 'Di', is the usual crossword former royal; the possessive S is used as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To leak information is to reveal it without authorisation, so both verbs mean make known what was secret.

clue.text: Unfortunate coital mishap, with young woman endlessly pulling out sausage

indicators.note: something unfortunate has gone wrong, so the letters fall into a new order
endless means without its end, so the last letter is cut
pulling something out removes it, so these letters are taken away

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, before trimming
a young woman is a miss; without its last letter it becomes three letters

explanation.surface: A bedroom accident involving withdrawal, with a sausage as the punchline.
explanation.walkthrough: Take MIS from 'mishap' to leave HAP, then rearrange COITAL and HAP. A chipolata is a small thin British sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: A chipolata is a particular kind of small, slender pork sausage, so it is an example of the category.

clue.text: A likely loser working for a bastard?

parts.note: to work for someone is to be under them
dog is slang for a contemptible man

explanation.surface: Anyone with a rotten boss is destined to lose out.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole second half reads as a comment on bad bosses, but it splits into two plain pieces: subordinate to, and a cur.
explanation.definitionFit: The underdog is the competitor expected to lose a contest, the one given little chance by bookmakers.

clue.text: Depraved TV presenter needs to get over a dip

parts.note: Declan Donnelly, Dec of the British presenting duo Ant and Dec
taken as written
a dent is a dip or hollow in a surface

explanation.surface: A disgraced TV presenter has to get past a slump in his career.
explanation.walkthrough: Ant and Dec are a hugely popular British TV presenting pair; in an across clue 'over' puts one piece before the next.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadent means morally decayed and self-indulgent, which is a synonym relation with corrupt or dissolute.

clue.text: Hell might be appalling

definitions.note: a gerund, read as a noun: the appalling of someone

parts.note: Dis is the classical underworld, in Dante the city of Hell
may and might are both modal verbs of possibility

explanation.surface: A warning that the underworld could turn out to be dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Might' looks like a verb in the sentence, and so it is, but as a synonym of 'may' rather than a statement about Hell.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismay is consternation and shock; appalling someone produces that feeling, so the noun sense of the gerund fits.

clue.text: Henry's thrown out gin-sozzled puss

indicators.note: someone sozzled is drunk and jumbled, so these letters are mixed up
what is thrown out is removed and no longer part of the whole

parts.note: Henry Kissinger, the US Secretary of State
taken as written; rearranged, it matches the middle of the surname

explanation.surface: Henry has kicked out his drunken cat.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry is Kissinger; 'gin' rearranged is ING, and removing it leaves KISSER. Both puss and kisser are slang for the face.
explanation.definitionFit: Puss and kisser are both informal slang terms for a person's face or mouth, a slang synonym.

clue.text: Is inside roped area, getting erect

indicators.note: inside places one part within the boundaries of another

parts.note: a boxing ring is an area enclosed by ropes
taken as written

explanation.surface: Another Private Eye innuendo, set in a boxing ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roped area' is the boxing ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming upright means going up from lying flat, so standing up and ascending describe the same motion.

clue.text: Spit on obstacle as an aid to drinking

parts.note: gob is British slang meaning to spit
a let is a hindrance, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: Spitting on a barrier somehow helps you drink.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second. 'Let' as obstacle survives in the legal phrase 'without let or hindrance'.
explanation.definitionFit: A goblet is a stemmed drinking vessel, so it is a container that helps a person take a drink.

clue.text: (+13 ac.) Oligarch might have been relieved of this terrible Cyprus heat

definitions.text: Oligarch might have been relieved of this

indicators.note: terrible suggests a dreadful mess, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written, ten letters

explanation.surface: A sweltering Mediterranean island, beloved of Russian money, where an oligarch had something confiscated.
explanation.walkthrough: After sanctions on Russia in 2022, many oligarchs had their luxury vessels seized.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge luxury private boat is the kind of asset authorities impounded from sanctioned Russian billionaires.

clue.text: Take steps to undo bra without a word of hesitation

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so one part surrounds another
undoing something takes it apart, so the letters are loosened and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
um is what people say while hesitating

explanation.surface: Advice on removing a bra confidently, without dithering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like 'lacking', but it means outside: the rearranged letters sit either side of UM.
explanation.definitionFit: To rumba is to perform a Latin ballroom dance, and dancing is literally taking steps to music.

clue.text: Fancy comic nose, not really Kwarteng's thing?

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate or fanciful, so the letters are dressed up in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A joke about a false comedy nose, and something the former Chancellor was not much good at.
explanation.walkthrough: Kwasi Kwarteng was the UK Chancellor whose 2022 mini-budget crashed the markets.
explanation.definitionFit: As Chancellor he ran the nation's finances, yet his budget caused turmoil, so the subject was hardly his strength.

clue.text: Sprog problem

definitions.meaning: first meaning: offspring; sprog is British slang for a child
second meaning: a difficulty or point of dispute

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like a troublesome child; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means children or descendants in legal language, and also a matter causing trouble or concern.

clue.text: Scared when singer Jones grabs member

indicators.note: to grab is to seize and hold, so one part holds another

parts.note: Aled Jones, the Welsh singer famous as a boy soprano
a member is a limb

explanation.surface: A fright when a crooner grabs someone's private parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singer Jones' tempts Tom Jones, but only Aled Jones gives the letters; 'member' is a limb, not the innuendo.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarmed means frightened or anxious at sudden danger, a straightforward synonym relation.

clue.text: 'Carry-on Sailing, Love' is out — no good

indicators.note: out as in out of order, so the letters are disarranged
no means none of, so the letter it qualifies is removed

parts.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A spoof Carry On film title that has been dropped as no good.
explanation.walkthrough: The Carry On films are a long series of British bawdy comedies; here 'carry-on' means an affair. Join SAILING and O, drop G, rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A carry-on in British slang is an illicit love affair, and a liaison is a secret sexual relationship.

clue.text: Frank mugged, so not smiling

parts.note: a straight answer is a frank one
mug is slang for face, so mugged can mean faced

explanation.surface: A man called Frank was robbed, so he is not smiling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frank' looks like a name and 'mugged' like a robbery; both are synonyms of the two parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping a straight face means showing no amusement, so the compound describes a solemn, expressionless look.
